Title: Numb, cold, or swollen hands and feet by evening? 3 foods quietly hurting your circulation

Description:
If your hands and feet feel numb, cold, or swollen by the end of the day, it might not just be "getting older" - a few everyday foods could be part of the problem.

Deli meat, fried food, and sugary soda are three of the biggest everyday culprits behind poor circulation, and each one has an easy swap that doesn't mean giving up flavor.

Watch to find out why these foods slow your circulation, and what to reach for instead.

platforms.title: It's Not Just Aging: What's Really Behind Numb, Swollen Hands and Feet
platforms.meta_description: Numb, cold, or swollen hands and feet aren't always just aging. Fatty broths, creamer coffee, and fruit juice can affect circulation and fluid balance.
platforms.body_html:
If your hands and feet feel numb, cold, or puffy by the end of the day, it's tempting to write it off as just getting older. But slowing circulation to the extremities is often tied to specific everyday habits, and three surprisingly common ones show up again and again: rich, slow-simmered broths, instant coffee loaded with powdered creamer, and a daily glass of fruit juice. Here's how each one quietly affects blood flow and fluid balance, and what tends to help instead.

The Saturated Fat Hiding in Slow-Simmered Broths

Homemade stocks and broths, the kind simmered for hours with bones, joints, or fatty cuts of meat, release rendered fat into the liquid as they cook. Chill a pot of stock overnight and that fat rises and solidifies into a pale layer on top, which is mostly saturated fat. A diet high in saturated fat contributes to atherosclerosis, the gradual buildup of fatty deposits along artery walls that narrows blood flow, including to the small vessels that supply the hands and feet. The American Heart Association recommends keeping saturated fat under 6% of daily calories for people trying to lower LDL cholesterol; for a 2,000-calorie diet, that's about 13 grams, an amount a single bowl of fatty broth-based soup can approach on its own.

Instant Coffee With Powdered Creamer

Powdered non-dairy creamers, the kind stirred into instant coffee, are often made mostly from palm oil, which is roughly half saturated fat by fatty acid composition. A few packets a day add up fast, especially when paired with salty snacks or processed sides. Sodium works differently from fat, but the two habits often travel together: eating too much salt makes the body hold onto extra water, which shows up as swelling in the hands, ankles, and feet. The Dietary Guidelines for Americans set the daily sodium limit at 2,300 milligrams, and the FDA notes that most Americans eat well above that.

Fruit Juice Isn't the Same as Whole Fruit

Juicing strips away most of the fiber in fruit, leaving behind a concentrated dose of sugar that the body absorbs much faster than it would from the whole fruit. A widely cited Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health study, published in 2013 in The BMJ, tracked more than 187,000 adults over roughly two decades and found that people who ate at least two servings a week of whole fruits like blueberries, grapes, and apples had up to a 23% lower risk of type 2 diabetes, while those who drank a serving of fruit juice daily had up to a 21% higher risk. Frequent blood sugar swings like this put extra stress on blood vessel walls over time.

Simple Swaps That Actually Help

  • Skim the fat before you eat it — Refrigerate homemade broth or stock overnight, then lift off the solidified fat layer with a spoon before reheating. Store-bought broths often list saturated fat per serving on the label, so choosing a lower-fat option works too.
  • Switch to a milk-based coffee — Swapping powdered creamer for low-fat milk, unsweetened soy milk, or simply black coffee cuts both the saturated fat and, often, the sodium hiding in flavored powders.
  • Eat the fruit instead of drinking it — Choosing whole fruit, or blending it into a smoothie with the pulp intact, keeps the fiber that slows sugar absorption.

The Bottom Line

None of these habits need to be cut out completely, and the swaps above are meant as substitutions, not restrictions. Paying attention to how broths, coffee creamer, and fruit are prepared can meaningfully ease the burden on circulation over time. This article is for general information only and isn't medical advice, so if numbness or swelling comes on suddenly or feels severe, it's worth checking with an internal medicine doctor.
